items.root_cause: Three mechanisms. (1) The fence vocabulary excludes the ADJECTIVE but not the CONTAINER or PREPARATION NOUN: jalapenos excludes canned, pickled, jar, sliced, but 'Can', 'Steel Can', 'escabeche' pass, so any canned produce named with the noun can win any fresh-produce commodity. (2) A store name that omits its type word defeats a type-word fence: GV 'Broccoli Florets' (frozen) carries no frozen or steam token, so first-match-wins hands it to fresh broccoli at index 50; the routing diff shows the same mechanism also parked two Armour Jalapeno Vienna Sausages and a GV Broccoli Stir-Fry blend plus a Kikkoman stir-fry seasoning packet on produce commodities. (3) Test-InStore's absence-is-not-a-verdict valve (correct for pre-field captures; shipped 08-31 in 23a20bd6) combined with the 90-day Walmart union means a ship-only product refused on its FRESH row still prices the board through its stale PRE-FIELD row, and BLANK-fulfillment rows inside a field-bearing capture (91 of 11,694, over half of them N-pack bundles) pass unchallenged.

SHIPPED: sync-recipesdb-cost.ps1 -Apply (the plan's command omitted -Apply, so the first run was read-only). Verified field by field against HEAD: exactly 3 fields on exactly 1 row, no-boil-chicken-pasta-casserole-with-artichokes-and-peas cost_batch_true 51.67 -> 51.59, cost_per_serving_true 3.69 -> 3.68, cost_first_run 55.54 -> 55.46. It did not drop the suffix - it changed all five authored specs FROM 'Artichoke Hearts, ...' TO 'Artichoke Hearts (Hannaford), ...', one line per file, and audit-db-agreement then reported issues=0. A green produced by writing the defect into the source of truth. (Note the plan's -Slugs invocation also needs a real array: passed through `powershell -File` the comma-separated list arrives as ONE string and the script dies with 'no specs matched'.) MECHANISM, proved from the source rather than inferred: head-ingredients-lib derives the JSON-LD list from ingredients_display and strips the brand parenthetical via Get-HiBrandSuffix, which returns ' (' + the CURRENT food-macros-db brand + ')' - by deliberate design, so that real parentheticals like 'BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free)' survive. The food DB row for 'Artichoke Hearts' was swapped from the Hannaford can to Great Value (its own notes field records 'The previous row was Hannaford'). Every display line built before that swap still carries ' (Hannaford)', which ' (Great Value)' cannot match, so the stale brand survives the strip and is written into the spec. EXPOSURE, measured with the estate's own derivation rather than a fourth copy of the rule: of 584 specs carrying a stored JSON-LD list, Get-HeadRecipeIngredient disagrees with the stored list on exactly 5, and all 5 differences are the derivation ADDING one parenthetical, always '(Hannaford)'. One food-DB row, five recipes, nothing else in the catalog exposed today. WHY IT IS A CLASS AND NOT A DETAIL: a strip keyed on the CURRENT value of a field cannot remove a value baked in under a PREVIOUS one, and here the disarmed rule does not merely stop protecting - the REPAIR built on it propagates the stale value into the authored source, and the paired audit reports CLEAN because it measures AGREEMENT, not correctness. repair-head-ingredients' own self-test asserts 'the JSON-LD list now matches the card line for line', so it cannot catch this either. A guard that can be satisfied by corrupting its own reference is different in kind from a rule that quietly stops firing. LEFT AS FOUND: the five drifts stand and audit-db-agreement is honestly RED at issues=5, exit 1. They are a wrong brand name on a card, not a wrong price. items.root_cause: the designed throttle valve - shard the term list ACROSS THE DAY - was never scheduled. No check watches that the intended cadence exists, so the missing cadence pages as catalog-degrading instead of as itself (rules-that-silently-disarm). Get-ScheduledTask returns exactly five tasks - TC Grocery Ad Pulls 0700, TC Grocery Daily Capture 0800, TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 0930, TC Graph Nightly Matching and TC Recipe Harvest Crawl - and there is NO 3-hourly Family Fare job. items.deviation: The root_fix as written could NEVER HAVE ARMED, and the prerequisite had to ship first. The plan says the cadence watcher should 'read the cursor-advance history'. That history is out\capture-cursor-log.jsonl, and Family Fare is not in it. Measured 2026-09-01: 17 Fareway advances, 11 Sam's Club, 11 Hy-Vee, 10 Baker's, 8 Walmart, 7 Aldi, and ZERO Family Fare - while its cursor sat at #600 and was plainly moving that morning. Cause: capture-policy-lib exposes Save-CaptureCursor (writes the cursor FILE, which holds only the latest value) and Write-CursorLog (appends the advance line) as TWO separate calls, every other rotation builder calls both, and pull-regular-familyfare called only the first. A watcher keyed on that log would have been silent forever - the gates-that-can-never-arm class. So the fix is three parts, not two: (1) pull-regular-familyfare now calls Write-CursorLog beside Save-CaptureCursor; (2) FF shard windows added to the 07:00 ad run (capture-run.ps1, deliberately OUTSIDE the store loop, because that loop only runs a store whose AD has rolled over, so an FF buy placed there would fire on rollover days rather than on a cadence) and to the 09:30 watchdog, giving three windows a day with no new scheduled task; (3) the MISSING-WINDOW watcher in capture-watchdog.ps1, built on a pure Measure-CursorAdvances so it is testable, with four frozen cases that pass: the real 1-window-a-day condition pages, three healthy windows stay silent, a log full of other stores reads as ZERO rather than as nothing-to-see, and an unparseable line is skipped rather than counted as a window. TEST-AUDITORS CAUGHT A REAL BUG IN THIS WORK, and it is worth recording rather than quietly fixing: the first draft of both shard invocations piped the child through 2>&1, and this estate sets EAP=Stop, which under PS 5.1 turns a native child's first stderr line into a terminating throw. That is the exact defect that made the 07:00 and 08:00 tasks exit 1 for weeks (fixed 2026-08-22). The tree scan flagged capture-run.ps1:481 before the line had ever run; all three of my call sites were corrected to capture the child's output into a variable with no redirect. NOT DONE: staggering the FF pull inside the 08:00 run so it does not share the exact minutes of the other six stores. The three windows are the arithmetic fix and they ship; the stagger is a launch-order change inside the parallel lane block and is the smaller half of the throttle question. MEASUREMENT THAT CLOSES THIS: within two days, re-verified-in-48h must climb back over the degradation floor from today's 10. The watcher itself will page MISSING-WINDOW tomorrow if either new window fails, which is the point - a dead window now pages as itself.
